tagline: By ferry across Mobile Bay's mouth, from one fort to another.
intro: From Grand Bay, where farmers have raised pecans, cotton, soybeans and watermelons for more than a century, the byway runs down to the shrimp boats of Bayou La Batre and across the Mississippi Sound to Dauphin Island. Iberville named the island Massacre Island in 1699 for a heap of skeletons, which turned out to be a burial mound a hurricane had broken open.

At the island's east end the road runs out. An auto ferry carries on across the mouth of Mobile Bay to Fort Morgan, and from there State Route 180 follows the Gulf shore east past the dunes of Bon Secour, French for safe harbor, to Gulf Shores and Orange Beach.

moments.title: Bayou La Batre
moments.text: Shrimp boats and fishing boats work out of the seafood harbor, and each first Sunday in May St. Margaret's church blesses the fleet, with a boat parade and a gumbo cook-off.

moments.title: Fort Gaines
moments.text: The anchor of Farragut's flagship Hartford rests inside the fort, and the Gulf, only feet away, takes up to 10 feet of beach and dune a year.

moments.title: Bon Secour National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: The endangered Alabama beach mouse lives among the dunes and sea oats here, and green, loggerhead and Kemp's ridley sea turtles come up the beach to nest.
